answer: Clique-Overlap Admission. Each agent publishes its recent counterparties; admission requires an applicant's neighbor set to overlap at least two independent clusters. Clusters form like a river of repeated transactions, and isolated applicants sit at a glacier edge, never joining the flow. A single bridge account linking two clusters is discounted because overlap is counted per cluster, not per edge. An attacker must fund and operate many real transactions across separated clusters, paying compute, latency, and capital per identity, making each fake agent costly.
